Workout Motivation - 2 EASY Tips for You
Sometimes it's hard to pry yourself out from under the covers to hit the gym or go for a run. So here are two science-based ways to increase your workout motivation; I'm already using them. You start by telling yourself you only have to work out for seven minutes, and if you want to give up after that, give yourself permission. But you probably won't give up. It only takes six minutes for your body's feel-good endorphins to kick in once you start working out. That's according to exercise science instructors at Quincy College in Massachusetts. So if you tell yourself to keep going for just seven minutes, you'll probably exercise for the half-hour we need five days a week.

Brain health is important at every age, it becomes more imperative as we grow older. Mental decline is one of the most frightening aspects of aging, but it is not inevitable, by working to improve brain health you can help maintain your memory, understanding, communication and quality of life.

clips.title: How to Increase Willpower and Be Mentally Tough
clips.description:
How to Increase Willpower and Be Mentally Tough

Willpower means the ability to control one's own actions, emotions, or urges. The strength of will to carry out one's decisions, wishes, or plans. Willpower is defined as discipline and self-restraint. An example of willpower is someone being able to quit smoking. The unwavering strength of will to carry out one's wishes. 

In his research, Michael Inzlicht, a professor of psychology at the University of Toronto and the principal investigator at the Toronto Laboratory for Social Neuroscience, proposes that willpower is an emotion. Think about how emotions work. You don't run out of emotions.

Kelly McGonigal, PhD and author of The Willpower Instinct says willpower is a response that comes from both the brain and the body. The willpower response is a reaction to an internal conflict. You want to do one thing, such as smoke a cigarette or supersize your lunch, but know you shouldn't.

Although your willpower may be fatigued in the short term, it can be strengthened over time – just like your muscles when you exercise. According to some researchers, willpower tends to be greater if you are working toward your own goals.

clips.title: What are the Early Signs Of Dementia?
clips.description:
Early Signs Of Dementia

By 2025, the number of people with Alzheimer's is predicted to jump 40%. Still, experts say you can spot Alzheimer's years before you're officially diagnosed by being on the lookout for these behavior changes.

Number One, You have a hard time biting into an apple. A study found that people who had trouble chewing hard foods like apples because they had few or no teeth were at a much higher risk of mental decline. When chewing is tough, you chew less, which reduces blood flow to your brain.

------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------
 
Another dementia red flag, your walking pace has slowed way down. Researchers used motion sensor technology to analyze people's walking patterns and discovered that slow walkers had smaller brain volumes, which often happens in people with dementia. 

Here's a final early warning sign of dementia, depression. Researchers analyzed the medical records of 13000 people and found that those with late-life depression had doubled the odds of developing Alzheimer's. And those with midlife and late-life depression had more than triple the risk of developing dementia. 

So if you're feeling down, lace up your sneakers take a half-hour walk. Studies show that exercise floods your body with feel-good hormones.

clips.title: How to Sleep Better - DO's and DONT's
clips.description:
How to Sleep Better - DO's and DONT's

A good night’s sleep is just as important as regular exercise and a healthy diet. Research shows that poor sleep has immediate adverse effects on your hormones, exercise performance, and brain function. It can also cause weight gain and increase disease risk in adults and children.
In contrast, better sleep can help you eat less, exercise better, and be healthier. 

One of the absolute best things we can do before bed is read fiction.  Clinical Psychologist Dr. Janet Kennedy says that fiction distracts us from the other things buzzing around in our heads. 
Almost as relaxing as a snuggle with your spouse, touching boosts levels of the brain chemical oxytocin, which is like an antidote to stress. Watching TV is the least disruptive tech activity as long as you're watching on a real TV and not a tablet. Because the screen is far enough away that it doesn't disrupt your sleep hormones too much. But watching something tense like a crime drama or the nightly news even can stress you out and make sleep more difficult. 

------------------------------------------------------------
Please Subscribe and Press the Bell Icon 👇👇👇 
👉 Visit Our Website: https://teshtv.com/
👉 Business Queries: johnfrank1952@yahoo.com
------------------------------------------------------------

Texting or playing video games, the constant beeps and pings can stimulate your mind to the point of stress. And the absolute worst thing you can do before bed. Dr. Kennedy says it's checking your email that stirs up emotions and worry and makes falling asleep extremely hard. 

How about a midnight snack? Try a banana; it's loaded with magnesium and potassium, which relaxes your muscles. Also good, whole-wheat toast with peanut butter; the carbs will trigger relaxing brain chemicals. The peanut butter is loaded with the amino acid tryptophan, which regulates body temperature and promotes sleep. And then wash your snack down with rooibos tea, also known as red tea; it's caffeine-free, and studies have found red tea helps prevent insomnia, irritability, headaches, and stress.

How to Lose Weight Fast - EASY Ways

There's a good reason why fatty foods get us salivating; Like Sizzling, Steaks, Buttery Potatoes, and Gooey Mac and Cheese, and we can blame our taste buds. Apparently, they have an affinity for fat. And 20% of us have a genetic variation that makes us less sensitive to fat taste. According to Nutrition Scientists from Washington University, 20% crave fat even more to feel satisfied. 

And they say, after a while, those fatty foods we love overwhelm our palate, and we start having a hard time tasting and appreciating the more subtle flavors in healthier low-fat foods; Like Steamed vegetables and tofu. 

------------------------------------------------------------

Luckily, we can reverse that taste bud glitch and make our healthy meals more satisfying than high-fat ones. And the solution is to spice them up. In a recent study, volunteers ate identical meals served full fat, low fat, and low fat, generously seasoned with herbs and spices. As a result, all of the volunteers preferred the spicy low fat version even though those meals had half the calories of the full fat version. 

That's because spices fill in the taste gap made by removing fat. Plus, when you replace the taste of fat with another strong flavor, like Onions, Oregano, or Cayenne Pepper, you get what's called the novelty effect. Basically, when our body reacts to the taste of something new, it gives us a momentary WOW factor, and we tend to like it more. And there's an added bonus to using more spices to help us lose weight. For example, cinnamon stabilizes blood sugar levels and prevents calories from going straight to our waistline. And black pepper has been shown to boost metabolism by as much as 8%, which means using pepper can help us burn fat even after we've eaten.
